contract.assumptions: The source limits the hardness claim to generic complex POVMs with variable dimensions. It does not assert hardness for transpose-compatible/restricted subclasses, fixed input dimension, equal-reference-marginal entropy order, numerical contraction coefficients, or a general Hermiticity-preserving-lift characterization. It gives no efficient witness-finding procedure. The status is a source claim, not an established or historically original theorem.
contract.provides: The manuscript claims coRE-completeness for complete SLD order on variable-dimensional rational-complex strictly positive POVM pairs, unrestricted complete Umegaki equivalence, no computable sufficient reference cutoff, and a fixed-additive-error obstruction for its bounded entropy defect. These claims are unreviewed; no theorem or novelty promotion is made.
contract.requires:
Each test is finite-dimensional, with dimensions not bounded uniformly over instances. A POVM E=(E_i) on C^a has positive effects summing to I_a; “strictly positive” means every E_i>0. The classified inputs are pairs of rational-complex strictly positive POVMs on a common input, where real and imaginary matrix entries are rational and the input dimension and outcome counts are part of the finite description.

For channels P,Q with common input, the note defines complete SLD order by comparison of the SLD quadratic forms for every finite untouched reference R, faithful input state rho, and traceless Hermitian tangent H. It defines unrestricted complete Umegaki relative-entropy order by D(P_R(alpha)||P_R(beta)) >= D(Q_R(alpha)||Q_R(beta)) for every finite R and every input-state pair alpha,beta; there is no equal-reference-marginal condition.

source_excerpts.text:
Undecidability of complete quantum
channel information order
A constructive reduction for rational strictly positive measurements
Prepared for Harjas Sandhu
10 October 2026
AI-generated mathematical research note
Not peer-reviewed. Originality and historical priority are unconfirmed.
Abstract
Complete symmetric logarithmic derivative information order is co-recursively enumer-
able complete, already for pairs of measurement channels specified by finite strictly positive
POVMs with rational complex entries. Its failure is recursively enumerable complete. The
same classification holds for unrestricted complete Umegaki relative-entropy order, in which
every finite untouched reference and every pair of input states are allowed. There is no
total computable bound, from a rational POVM pair, on a reference dimension sufficient
to detect every failure of complete SLD order.
The proof reduces the finite-dimensional nonlocal-game promise supplied byMIP∗ = RE
to a uniformly gapped polynomial on the actual two-factor normalized Jordan domain. A
quantitative Pauli anchor and local completely positive smoothing establish soundness. An
ordered-word graph construction compiles the polynomial to inverse-Jordan kernels, which
are embedded into normalized strictly positive POVMs with a dimension-independent
global completion. All these reduction steps, and the equivalence between the two channel
orders, are proved below. The nonlocal-game hardness theorem is the external complexity
premise. A further normalization using its perfect consistent strategies gives a computable
positive entropy margin. Finite tensor amplification then proves that the bounded complete
entropy defect cannot be uniformly approximated even at the fixed additive error1/4.

statement:
1. For the rational strictly positive POVM-pair class above, complete SLD dominance is coRE-complete under computable many-one reductions; failure is RE-complete.
2. For every finite-dimensional channel pair, complete SLD order is equivalent to the stated unrestricted complete Umegaki relative-entropy order. Consequently the same coRE/RE classification applies to that POVM class and entropy order.
3. No total computable function of a valid rational POVM pair bounds a reference dimension sufficient to witness every failure of complete SLD order.
4. For strictly positive POVMs the manuscript defines a finite bounded entropy defect V(E,F). It claims no total algorithm approximates V at every requested rational additive tolerance, and that even additive error 1/4 is impossible uniformly over the same rational-complex strictly positive POVM class. The fixed-error claim uses a computable positive witness margin and finite tensor amplification; it is not presented as an efficiency result.
title: Complete quantum channel information order is coRE-complete for rational positive POVMs
